transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t seem to get away from these awful thoughts that I’ve missed something important—like, critically important. It’s not just “oh, I forgot something,” it’s more like this sudden certainty, or maybe not certainty, but this unbearable possibility, that I made one wrong entry in a data release, or put the wrong number somewhere, and then that could cause some huge problem. Or I’ll leave the house and think, “What if the back door wasn’t locked?” even if I remember checking it. Or I’ll pay a bill and then get stuck thinking maybe I used the wrong account and now something is going to bounce or I’ve created some mess I won’t find out about until it’s too late.

And the thing is, I know—at least part of me knows—that I checked. I can remember checking. But my mind just won’t let it go. It keeps coming back to, “But what if you missed it? What if this is the one time you caused a disaster?” It’s exhausting, and honestly I’m here because I don’t feel like I can trust my own sense that something is done anymore.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions over and over, like checking the door or re-verifying your work, in an attempt to alleviate these thoughts?

Yes. I do, a lot. It’s not just once or twice, either. If it’s work, I’ll reopen the same spreadsheet after I’ve already closed it and go back through the entries, and then I’ll think, “Well, maybe I only looked at it, I didn’t really verify it,” so I start again. I’ll reread emails line by line, sometimes more than once, looking for whether I attached the right file or typed the wrong number or said something that could be misunderstood.

And at home it’s similar. I check the locks, but not just casually—I end up doing it in this certain order, like front door, back door, side door, then I’ll circle back because if I don’t do it the right way it doesn’t feel settled. Same with payment confirmations. I’ll pull them up again and again to make sure it went through and that the account or amount was right.

It does calm me down for a moment, but only for a moment. Then the doubt comes back, and I feel like I have to check again until it feels safe. Some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, and the awful part is I haven’t actually finished anything new—I’ve just been rechecking the same things over and over.
Do you feel anxious or on edge when you're not experiencing these specific thoughts about missing something important?

I’m not completely sure how to separate it out, honestly. It feels like most of the time when I’m anxious, it does eventually attach itself to one of those thoughts—like something unfinished, something I missed, something I should go back and verify.

If you mean, am I just generally on edge for no reason when none of that is happening… I don’t know. I haven’t really tracked it that way. I think I can have moments where I’m not actively thinking about a specific mistake, but I’m still kind of braced, like waiting for that feeling to show up again. But I can’t say clearly whether that’s a separate anxiety or just the after-effect of being stuck in that loop so much.

So… I guess the honest answer is I’m not sure. I mostly notice the anxiety when it’s tied to the checking and the “what if I missed something” thoughts.
Do you feel anxious when you're not thinking about making a mistake or missing something important?

I don’t really know. I mean, I’m trying to think about it, and it’s hard because the anxiety is so tied up with that mistake-or-missed-something feeling that I don’t always catch where it starts.

There are times when I’m not actively thinking, “I entered the wrong number” or “I left something unlocked,” and I might still feel sort of tense or unsettled, but then if I sit with it for more than a minute my brain usually finds something to attach it to. So I can’t honestly say, yes, I’m anxious totally separate from that, because it almost always seems to circle back there.

Maybe I’m on edge in between, like I’m waiting for the next thing I’m supposed to worry about, but I don’t know if that counts as anxiety on its own or just leftover from the checking and second-guessing. I haven’t really been able to separate it cleanly.
Is there ever a time when you feel anxious without any thoughts of making a mistake or missing something?

I’m honestly not sure. I keep trying to answer it cleanly, like yes or no, but when I look at my actual experience it gets muddled almost immediately.

There might be little stretches where I feel uneasy and I’m not consciously thinking, “I made a mistake,” or “I missed something,” but it’s hard to know whether that’s really separate. Because once I notice the anxious feeling, my mind almost starts searching for a reason, and very quickly it lands on something I should check or something I might have overlooked. So by the time I’m aware of the anxiety, it’s already wrapped around that kind of thought.

I don’t think I’ve really noticed many times where I’m just anxious in a totally blank way, with no connection to that. Or if it happens, I don’t recognize it before it turns into the usual worry. So I guess the best I can say is… I don’t know. I can’t confidently say that I do.
Can you recall any recent situation where you felt anxious without having any thoughts about making a mistake or missing something?

I’m trying to think of one, and I can’t really pull up a clear example. Not one where I could say, “Yes, that was anxiety, and it had nothing to do with possibly making a mistake or missing something.”

Like, if I think about this past week, there were moments where I felt physically tense or uneasy, but as soon as I try to examine it, I’m not sure what came first. I might not have had a specific thought right at the very beginning, but then almost immediately my mind starts reviewing things—what did I do, did I send something wrong, did I forget to check something, did I overlook a detail. So it becomes connected to that pretty fast.

I guess I haven’t noticed a recent situation where it stayed separate. If it happens, I either don’t catch it early enough, or I don’t remember it because it gets swallowed up by the usual “what if I missed something” feeling. So… no, I can’t recall a clean example right now.
Do you have any other repetitive behaviors or rituals that you feel compelled to perform, aside from checking and rechecking your work or locks?

Yes… I mean, aside from the obvious checking locks, it’s not always a totally different ritual, but it becomes this whole sequence I feel like I have to do.

With spreadsheets, for example, I’ll reopen the same file after I’ve already closed it, sometimes several times, and I’ll go back through the numbers or formulas in the same order. It’s not just “let me take one last look.” It feels like I have to start from the beginning again, because if I jump around, then I don’t trust it. And emails are similar—I’ll reread them line by line, slowly, even after I know what they say, because I’m afraid I missed a word or a wrong attachment or something that changes the whole meaning.

Payments are another one. If I pay a bill or submit something online, I’ll keep going back to the confirmation page or the email receipt, checking the amount, the account, the date, the confirmation number. And I tend to do it in this set order, like amount first, then recipient, then date, then confirmation, and if I get interrupted or feel like I didn’t really “see” it properly, I start again.

The thing is, I’m not doing it because it’s useful by that point. I’m doing it until it feels safe enough to stop. And sometimes that “safe” feeling just doesn’t come, so I can still be sitting at my desk hours later, with everything open again, rereading and reopening things, and somehow nothing is actually finished.
Have your symptoms of checking and worrying about mistakes interfered with your ability to work or maintain relationships?

Yes. Very much, unfortunately.

Work is probably the clearest place. I’ve fallen behind on major deadlines because I can’t get through things in a normal amount of time. I’ll tell myself I’m just going to review something once more, but then I end up staying late going over the same spreadsheet or document again and again, and somehow I still don’t feel finished. So it’s this awful thing where I’m putting in extra hours, but I’m not actually producing more. I’m just stuck reviewing.

And then by the time I should send something or move on to the next part, I’m exhausted, or it’s too late, or I’ve used up all the time I had. So deadlines that should have been manageable become these huge problems.

It’s affected my personal life too. I used to go to salsa nights, and I used to kayak, and I’ve stopped doing those things a lot of the time because I can’t get away from the checking and reviewing in time. I’ll think, “Okay, I’ll leave in twenty minutes,” and then two hours later I’m still at my desk trying to make sure I didn’t miss something. By then it’s too late to go, or I’m so drained that I just don’t.

So yes, it’s definitely interfering. It feels like my life keeps getting narrower because I can’t finish things and walk away from them.
Do you feel like your symptoms of checking and worrying are causing you a lot of emotional pain or distress?

Yes. It’s… it’s causing a lot of distress. That’s really why I came in, because I feel like my mind is constantly grabbing onto these awful possibilities and not letting me put them down.

It’ll be something like, what if there’s a wrong number in a data release, and then someone uses it and it causes some huge problem. Or I’ll think, what if the back door wasn’t actually locked, even though I checked it. Or what if I paid a bill from the wrong account, or entered the wrong amount, and somehow that leads to a mess I can’t undo. And the horrible part is that even when I can remember checking, it doesn’t feel like enough. My mind says, “But what if you only thought you checked? What if you missed the one critical thing?”

It’s not just ordinary concern. It feels like this sharp, relentless fear that I’ve caused a disaster or am about to cause one because I missed some tiny detail. And I know from the outside it may sound excessive, because sometimes I can even tell myself, “You already looked at this,” but emotionally it doesn’t settle. I keep feeling responsible, like if I stop checking or stop thinking about it, then I’m being careless.

So yes, it’s very painful. It’s exhausting, and it makes me feel trapped in my own head.
Is there ever a moment when you feel anxious without any thought or concern about making a mistake or missing something?

Honestly, not very often. I mean, I do feel anxious, but when I really slow down and look at it, it almost always has some thread of, “What if I missed something?” or “What if I made some mistake and now there’s going to be a consequence?”

That’s sort of what brought me in. I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical—like a wrong number in a data release, or that the back door wasn’t actually locked, or that I paid a bill from the wrong account. And even if I can remember checking it, even if I know logically that I checked it, my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I somehow caused a disaster or failed to prevent one.

So if you’re asking whether I get anxiety that feels totally separate from that… I’m sure maybe I have moments of general tension, but the distressing anxiety, the kind that takes over, is usually tied to that fear that I missed something important. It’s like everything circles back to that.
Can you think of any situation where you felt anxious without having any thoughts about making a mistake or missing something?

I’m trying to think of one, and honestly… no, not really—not the kind that really grabs me.

I mean, I can get tense in a general way, I suppose, but when I look closely at the anxiety that actually feels overwhelming, it almost always has that same shape to it. It’s some version of, “What if I missed something important?” or “What if I made a mistake and now something bad is going to happen because of me?”

That’s really what made me come in. I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. Like at work, I’ll think maybe there’s a wrong number in a data release, and then I imagine people using it and everything going wrong because I didn’t catch it. Or at home, it’s the back door—what if it wasn’t actually locked, even though I checked it? Or with bills, I’ll think, what if I paid it from the wrong account or entered the wrong amount and now I’ve created some mess.

And the part that scares me is that even when I know I checked—like I can remember checking—it still doesn’t feel settled. My mind keeps saying, “But what if you missed the one thing that mattered?” So I can’t really think of a situation where the anxiety is totally separate from that. It always seems to come back to the possibility that I caused or failed to prevent some disaster.
Is it possible for you to feel anxious without any thoughts about making a mistake or missing something, even for a brief moment?

Maybe for a split second, like just a general body feeling of being keyed up, but if I actually pay attention to what’s underneath it, it almost immediately attaches to that same fear. It’s like I can’t separate the anxiety from the thought that I missed something or made some mistake.

That’s why I came in, really. I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical—like a wrong number in a data release at work, or that the back door wasn’t actually locked, or that I paid a bill from the wrong account or entered the wrong amount. And even when I know I checked it, even when I can picture myself checking it, my mind just won’t let go. It keeps asking, “But what if you’re wrong? What if this is the time you caused a disaster?”

So… possible for a brief moment, maybe in the most technical sense. But the anxiety that bothers me, the one that takes over, is almost always tied to that fear that I missed something important.
Do you ever feel anxious in social situations without thinking about making a mistake or missing something?

In social situations… I mean, I do get anxious around people sometimes, but when I really look at what I’m anxious about, it still tends to become that same thing. It’s not usually just, “Oh, people are looking at me,” or something separate like that. It becomes, “What if I said the wrong thing?” or “What if I forgot something important?” or “What if I missed some detail and now there’s going to be a consequence?”

But the main examples—the ones that really stick and loop in my head—are more like work or home things. I came in because I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. Like a wrong number in a data release, and then I imagine all the damage that could happen because I didn’t catch it. Or the back door—I’ll think maybe it wasn’t actually locked, even if I remember checking it. Or a bill, like maybe I paid it from the wrong account or entered something incorrectly.

And even when I know I checked, it doesn’t feel finished. My mind just keeps going back to, “But what if you caused a disaster?” So in social situations, if I’m anxious, it usually still hooks onto that kind of fear somehow. I can’t really think of it being totally separate.
Can you describe any recent situation where you felt anxious without immediately thinking about a potential mistake or something you might have missed?

I’m trying to think of a recent time, and… not really, not in a clean way. There might be this very brief flash where I just feel anxious physically, like my chest tightens or I get keyed up, but almost immediately my mind goes to, “What did I miss?” or “What did I do wrong?”

The reason I came in is because that pattern keeps happening with these really upsetting, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. At work it might be a number in a data release—like I’ll suddenly think, “What if one value was wrong and people are using it now?” And then I start imagining consequences from that. At home it’s the back door, like even if I remember checking it, I’ll think, “But what if it wasn’t really locked?” Or with bills, I’ll worry I paid from the wrong account or entered the wrong amount and created some serious problem.

So if you’re asking whether I can remember feeling anxious recently without that attaching to it… I can’t really give you a good example. Even when I know I checked something, my mind won’t let go of the possibility that I caused some kind of disaster. That’s the part that feels so exhausting—it doesn’t stay as just anxiety. It turns into this loop about a mistake or something I missed.
Do you ever feel anxious when you're alone, without thinking about making a mistake or missing something?

Yes, definitely when I’m alone too. Honestly, being alone doesn’t really make it separate from the mistake fear. If anything, that’s when it can get louder because there’s nothing else pulling my attention away from it.

I’ll be sitting by myself and suddenly it’s like my brain throws something at me—“What if that number in the data release was wrong?” And then I’m replaying whether I checked it, whether I looked at the right column, whether I might have missed one entry. Or I’ll be at home alone and think, “Is the back door actually locked?” even if I can remember checking it. Or I’ll think about a bill and wonder if I paid it from the wrong account or typed the wrong amount.

So I do feel anxious alone, but I can’t really say it’s without those thoughts. It almost always turns into this awful, unwanted thought that I missed something critical, and even when part of me knows I checked it, my mind won’t let go. It keeps circling back to, “What if you caused some disaster and just don’t know it yet?”
Is there ever a situation where you feel anxious and it doesn't involve thinking you've made a mistake or missed something?

I’m honestly trying to find one, but I don’t think so—not really. If I feel anxious, it almost always gets tied to this idea that I’ve made some mistake or missed something important.

Like, the thing that made me come in is these awful unwanted thoughts that I missed something critical. At work, it’s a wrong number in a data release, and then I start imagining that people are using the wrong information and it’s somehow my fault. At home it can be the back door, like I’ll know I checked it, but then my mind says, “What if it wasn’t actually locked?” Or with bills, I’ll worry I paid one from the wrong account or entered something wrong.

And the frustrating part is that even when I know I checked, it doesn’t settle. It’s like my mind won’t accept it. It keeps going back to, “What if you caused a disaster?” So I can’t really think of a situation where the anxiety is just anxiety and doesn’t involve that fear in some way.
Do you feel anxious when engaging in hobbies or leisure activities without thinking about making a mistake or missing something?

Yes… even with hobbies or things that are supposed to be relaxing, it doesn’t really stay separate from that fear. I might sit down to do something just for myself, and for a minute I’m trying to enjoy it, but then my mind jumps back to, “Did I miss something?” or “What if there was some critical mistake I didn’t catch?”

It’s usually the same kinds of things I’ve mentioned. A wrong number in a data release at work, like I’ll suddenly picture that one value being off and people relying on it. Or I’ll be at home trying to unwind and then I’m thinking about the back door—“Did I actually lock it, or do I just think I did?” Or a bill, where I start wondering if I paid it from the wrong account or entered the amount wrong.

And even if I can tell myself, “No, I checked that,” it doesn’t really land. My mind keeps circling back to the possibility that I caused some disaster and I just haven’t found out yet. So I do feel anxious during leisure time, but I can’t honestly say it’s without those thoughts. They kind of intrude on it.
Do you ever feel anxious when you are with close friends or family without thinking about making a mistake or missing something?

Not really, no. I mean, I can be sitting with my family or talking with a close friend, and on the outside I probably look like I’m listening or participating, but inside my mind will suddenly latch onto the same thing—some possibility that I missed something important.

It’s like I’ll be mid-conversation and then I’ll think, “What if that number in the data release was wrong?” And then I’m half there with the person and half replaying what I checked, whether I looked at the right version, whether there was one entry I skipped over. Or if I’m at home with family, I might start thinking about the back door again—“Did I really lock it, or am I just remembering that I meant to lock it?” And then it’s hard to stay present because the thought feels urgent, like if I don’t figure it out, something terrible could happen.

Same with bills. I can be with someone I trust, having what should be a normal, comfortable moment, and suddenly I’m wondering if I paid from the wrong account or typed the wrong amount. And even if I tell myself, “You checked it,” it doesn’t quiet down the way I think it should. My mind just keeps pushing, “But what if you caused a disaster and you don’t know yet?”

So being with close friends or family helps a little in the sense that I’m not physically alone, but it doesn’t make the anxiety become separate from those thoughts. If I’m anxious, it’s almost always because that fear has gotten in there somehow.
Is it ever possible for you to feel anxious without any thoughts about making a mistake or missing something?

I don’t think so. I’ve been trying to separate it out, but when I look closely, the anxiety is almost always attached to that same kind of thought—that I made some mistake, or missed something I should have caught.

That’s really why I came in. I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that something critical slipped past me. Like at work, it’ll be a wrong number in a data release, and I’ll start thinking people are going to use bad information because of me. Or at home, it’s the back door—like I know I checked it, but then my mind says, “What if you didn’t really lock it?” Or with a bill, I’ll worry I paid it from the wrong account or entered something wrong.

And the part that feels so exhausting is that checking doesn’t really end it. Even when I know I checked, even when I can remember checking, my mind won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some kind of disaster. So, no… I can’t really think of anxiety that’s just there on its own, without those thoughts wrapped around it.
Is it possible for you to experience anxiety without it being about making a mistake or missing something?

No, I don’t think it really is. I keep trying to think of an example where I’m just anxious in a general way, but when I trace it back, it almost always has that same theme underneath it—that I’ve made some mistake or missed something important.

That’s honestly why I came in. I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that something critical slipped past me. At work, it might be a wrong number in a data release, and then I’m imagining people using that information and everything going wrong because of me. At home it can be the back door, like I’ll know I checked it, but then my mind says, “But what if you didn’t really lock it?” Or with a bill, I’ll start worrying I paid it from the wrong account or entered the amount wrong.

And even when I know I checked it, it doesn’t feel settled. My mind keeps coming back to the possibility that I caused some disaster and just haven’t found out yet. So, no… I can’t really separate the anxiety from those thoughts.
